links.outcome: Characterization of identified safety concerns by LLM vs clinician intake interviewers in simulated patient interviews
links.effect: LLM characterized identified safety concerns less often than clinicians (33.3% vs. 66.7%).
links.quote: the LLM recovered more of the clinically relevant items embedded in the patient vignettes (88.0% vs. 38.9%), but made more clinical inferences not based on the interview (56.8% vs. 27.8%), and characterized identified safety concerns less often (33.3% vs. 66.7%)

links.outcome: Clinical inferences not based on the interview (ungrounded content) by LLM vs clinicians
links.effect: LLM made more clinical inferences not based on the interview than clinicians (56.8% vs. 27.8%).
links.quote: the LLM recovered more of the clinically relevant items embedded in the patient vignettes (88.0% vs. 38.9%), but made more clinical inferences not based on the interview (56.8% vs. 27.8%), and characterized identified safety concerns less often (33.3% vs. 66.7%)

unlisted_practices: Clinician-grounded quality assurance platform using memory-augmented simulated patients to compare AI and clinician interviewing approaches for psychiatric intake

screen.reason: Evaluates a clinician-grounded simulation platform (InterviewPlayground) designed as a deployment QA safeguard/testing mechanism for evaluating AI psychiatric intake systems prior to patient-facing rollout.

primary.practice: simulated-patient quality assurance testing prior to deployment
